mentor.diagnosis: You lost time working out what an acronym meant instead of answering the question. The exam never expands them, and a stem you have to decode twice is a stem you answer slowly and badly.
contrast: It is a RATE, so it multiplies. Once in four years is 0.25, not 4
SINGLE: one event, not a year
A point in the past: how much data you can lose
A duration forward: how long until you are back
To repair: how long a fix takes
mentor.rule: Expand the acronym in your head and the answer is usually inside the words. Rate multiplies, point looks backwards, time looks forwards, single means one event.
mentor.tell: Any stem with a bare three-letter acronym and numbers in the options is testing whether you know which word the acronym hides.
mentor.trap: The ones that catch people are the pairs that differ by one word: SLE and SLA, RPO and RTO, MTBF and MTTR, DAC and MAC. Learning the pair together is faster than learning either alone.
